paragraphs: The Z4 sDrive20i has been part of the Z4 range since 2002, and across its three generations has used three different engines — from the N52 through to today's B48. Early cars (E85 generation, 2002–2008) used the N52 — a 2.5-litre naturally aspirated inline-six. The E89 generation (2009–2016) switched to the N20, a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder. The current G29 generation (2018–present) uses the B48, a more recent 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder that's a different unit entirely. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and rebuild specifics differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The Z4 sDrive20i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

compatibility.intro: Because the Z4 sDrive20i spans three distinct engines across three generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N20 part will work on a B48 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:
